# Dushun (attributed) — The Jewel Net of Indra (Cleary, 2000)

## Bibliographic identity

The selected English carrier is Thomas Cleary's translation of “The Jewel Net of Indra,” printed under Tu-shun's name in *Dharma Rain*, pages 58–60. Kaza and Kraft drew the excerpt from Cleary's *Entry into the Inconceivable: An Introduction to Hua-yen Buddhism* (University of Hawai‘i Press, 1983), 66–68; that earlier container will receive its own source house if the essay cites material beyond this excerpt. The underlying Chinese passage belongs to the *Huayan wujiao zhiguan* (華嚴五教止觀, *Calming and Contemplation in the Five Teachings of Huayan*), conventionally attributed to Dushun (557–640), at Taishō canon T45, no. 1867, 513a28–513b21. Modern scholarship disputes that attribution, so the record preserves it as conventional provenance rather than settled authorship.

## Essay use

### Source's relevant contribution

The passage makes each jewel of Indra's net a site in which the remaining jewels appear, then follows the reflections recursively so that the whole net is implicated within every local jewel. This is the primary-text pathway for the essay's image of a field whose members disclose one another through their relations.

### Licensed essay use

- Establish the jewel-net as a Huayan image of reciprocal reflection and recursive implication.
- Give the myth history a textual route from the Indian figure of Indra into Chinese Huayan philosophical elaboration.
- Place the image beside Hephaestus's bonds as the source-bearing half of the essay's Offered double-net reading.

### Claim boundary

This passage does not derive apoha, Nāgārjuna's account of dependent arising, Kashmir Śaiva *saṃkalpa*, QL's `0/1`, or a theory of digital networks and commons governance. Those relations must be argued across their own sources. The Dushun attribution remains conventional and contested, and Cleary's printed pages must be collated before any English wording is promoted as quotation-ready.

## Passage card — `dushun-cleary-2000-jewel-net-indra-q001` — every jewel contains the net
^dushun-cleary-2000-jewel-net-indra-q001

**Source-matched paraphrase:** Each jewel reflects the jewels throughout the net, and those reflections contain further reflections without exhaustion; a local member therefore discloses the field through which it is locally distinct.

- **Locator:** Cleary trans., pp. 58–60; Chinese basis T45, no. 1867, 513a28–513b21.
- **Status:** source-matched; selected-edition collation required before quotation.
- **Verification:** Coordinator, 2026-07-16; work identity, page span, and Taishō locator checked; exact English wording withheld pending inspection of the selected printed edition.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** primary-text provenance for recursive jewel-net reflection.

- **Use boundary:** establishes the Huayan image's own recursive operation; it does not itself state the essay's Buddhist braid, opposed-net mytheme, or governance claims.

## Complete contemplative continuation — primary Chinese control

The Chinese sequence was recovered directly from the [CBETA XML transcription](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cbeta-org/xml-p5/master/T/T45/T45n1867.xml) on 2026-09-08. The full research copy of T45 no. 1867 (`working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/huayan-wujiao-zhiguan-cbeta/T45n1867.xml`) and a line-labelled extraction of 513a20–513c18 (`working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/huayan-wujiao-zhiguan-cbeta/0513a20-0513c18.txt`) retain the recovered object. The extraction is a reading aid and may include apparatus readings; the XML remains the control. Neither object is a collation of Cleary’s printed English or a Taishō page image.

| Chinese locator | Source-matched paraphrase and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| 513a20–27 | The knowing relation introduces mutual entry and the universal-eye field before the jewel-net image. |
| 513a28–513b21 | Clear jewels reflect one another recursively. A southwest jewel provides a definite entry; remaining there permits entry into all. The one/many questions follow the operation, rather than adding a privileged centre. The older source locator ends within the continuing dialogue. |
| 513b21–513c3 | The ink-dot test makes one particular marking appear throughout the reflected field. A different starting jewel permits the same traversal. |
| 513c4–10 | The teaching explicitly qualifies its simile: jewels’ images enter one another while their substances remain distinct; the phenomena being taught interpenetrate more fully. Partial resemblance is stated within the source itself. |
| 513c11–18 | Closing Vairocana verses direct manifestation toward beings, followed by the closing title and Dushun attribution. This copied attribution does not resolve the historical authorship dispute. |

The [complete Indra-net whole](../../../../../mytheme/worlds/chinese-huayan/indra-net/WHOLE.md#indra-simile-and-distinctness) **consumes** the continuation through the ink mark, source qualification and closing orientation. The selected Cleary excerpt retains its existing bibliographic identity and English quotation debt. The broader Chinese span supports the full contemplative aftermath without certifying that the anthology’s excerpt includes every sentence in the same wording.
